questions.prompt: Who can access a file uploaded with Anthropic's Files API, according to its docs?

options.text: Only the end user who uploaded it, nobody else.
options.explanation: The page says files are not limited to an end user, conversation or session.

options.text: Only the conversation it was uploaded in.
options.explanation: Files are not tied to one conversation. They belong to the workspace.

options.text: Any API key with access to that workspace.
options.explanation: Right. That is why the page says to keep separate data in separate workspaces.

questions.prompt: What does Anthropic's prompt-injection guide mean by "indirect prompt injection"?

options.text: Hidden instructions in content the model reads, like an email or a file.
options.explanation: Right. The user is trusted, but the content they bring in may not be.

options.text: A user who asks the same banned question many times, in new words each time.
options.explanation: The guide treats attacks by the user under jailbreaks and direct injection.

options.text: A developer who changes the system prompt without a code review.
options.explanation: That is a process problem, not what the guide calls indirect prompt injection.

questions.prompt: Your app filters search by team. Where should the team value come from?

options.text: From a team name the user types into the question.
options.explanation: A user could type any team, including HR.

options.text: From the user's login, set by the application.
options.explanation: Right. The user can't change it, so the filter actually limits access.

options.text: From the model, which guesses the team from the question.
options.explanation: A guess is not an access control. OpenAI's agent safety guide says a model can leak private data in a way that's not intended, without an attacker behind it.
